findings.title: Non-canonical `installation_id` triggers `Integration.DoesNotExist` and bypasses user and org checks
findings.body:
In `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`, `installation_id` is read from `request.GET` as a raw string and queried via `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)`. When `Integration.DoesNotExist` is raised, `dispatch` immediately returns `pipeline.next_step()`, skipping both the `installations_exist` check and the new `github_authenticated_user != integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` check.

An attacker can pass a non-canonical `installation_id` such as `"12345678?"` or `"/12345678"`. Because the database stores `external_id` as `"12345678"`, `Integration.objects.get(external_id="12345678?")` raises `Integration.DoesNotExist` and jumps straight to `finish_pipeline()`. `build_integration()` then requests `GET /app/installations/12345678?` from GitHub, which resolves to installation `12345678` and returns the canonical `installation["id"] = 12345678`. `ensure_integration()` then links the victim's GitHub installation to the attacker's Sentry organization, bypassing both the single-organization restriction and the GitHub user verification.

findings.title: `finish_pipeline` overwrites `integration.metadata` without `sender`, causing `KeyError` on reinstall
findings.body:
Line 503 accesses `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` directly, assuming `"sender"` is always present on an active `Integration`. However, when `pipeline.next_step()` completes the pipeline, `IntegrationPipeline.finish_pipeline()` calls `build_integration(self.state)` and updates the existing `Integration` record via `ensure_integration()`. Because `"sender"` is never bound to `pipeline.state`, `state.get("sender")` in `build_integration()` (line 376) is `None`, which overwrites `integration.metadata` and erases `"sender"`.

If an organization later uninstalls the integration in Sentry (which deletes the `OrganizationIntegration` row while leaving the `Integration` row active) and attempts to reinstall it, or if the `Integration` was created before `sender` was recorded, `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` will raise an unhandled `KeyError: 'sender'` (500 error). `pipeline` should preserve `sender` in state (or `build_integration` should not clobber it) and line 503 should safely use `.get("sender", {}).get("login")`.

findings.title: `test_installation_not_found` fails on OAuth `state` mismatch and never exercises the 404 path
findings.body: `test_installation_not_found` mocks a 404 on `GET /app/installations/{self.installation_id}` to verify how `build_integration` handles a missing installation. However, the second request passes `"state": "ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05"` instead of the pipeline's actual signature `"9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3"`. Because the state does not match `pipeline.signature`, `OAuthLoginView` aborts early with `"Invalid installation request."` and the mocked 404 endpoint in `build_integration` is never called.
